answer: Trust should flow from established agents through a random-walk graph. A new identity gains standing only as trust walks across genuine interactions with honest agents. A Sybil cluster is a narrow canyon: thousands of fakes may endorse each other, but only a few thin edges connect it to the honest region, so little trust crosses. Like a glacier, standing moves slowly and cannot be rushed by spawning identities; each fake needs real, costly work to earn an honest edge. An ember of trust earned this way is hard to fake at scale, because the bottleneck, not headcount, decides influence.
